endpoints.description: The EQ-5D-5L questionnaire visual analogue scale (VAS) measures overall health status on a vertical VAS ranging from 0 to 100. A higher score indicates better quality of life. The change from baseline in the EQ-5D-5L VAS score will be determined.

endpoints.measure: Change in the EQ-5D-5L Index Scores
endpoints.time_frame: Baseline and up to 18 months after CSL222 treatment
endpoints.description: The EQ-5D-5L questionnaire descriptive system of health-related quality of life consists of 5 dimensions (mobility, self-care, usual activities, pain/discomfort, anxiety/depression) for which responses will be recorded on 5 levels of severity (no problems, slight problems, moderate problems, severe problems, and extreme problems). The responses will be converted into a single index utility score (typically between -0.6 and 1). A higher score indicates better quality of life. The change from baseline in the EQ-5D-5L index score will be determined.

outcome.rationale: HOPE-B trial demonstrated etranacogene dezaparvovec efficacy and safety in hemophilia B, including in AAV5 NAb-positive subgroup (titers ≤678). NCT06003387 specifically enrolls NAb-positive patients with expected similar efficacy profile. Primary endpoint (ABR reduction) highly likely to be met based on mechanistic consistency and prior trial data. Safety profile well-characterized and manageable.

value.uncertainty: Extrapolation from HOPE-B NAb-negative data to NAb-positive population; single-arm design without concurrent control; actual results may vary based on NAb titer distribution

analysis_trace: Trial NCT06003387 is a Phase 3b open-label single-dose study of CSL222 (etranacogene dezaparvovec) in adults with hemophilia B who have pretreatment AAV5 neutralizing antibodies (NAb). The primary endpoint is ABR during months 7-18 post-treatment.

Evidence base: HOPE-B trial (NCT03569891) demonstrated etranacogene dezaparvovec efficacy in hemophilia B. Key publication (PMC12857339) shows in NAb-negative participants (N=33), mean ABR was 0.57 during months 7-48 vs 3.80 during lead-in (P<0.0001). Year 1 ABR was 0.99.

AAV5 NAb subgroup analysis from HOPE-B (2026 publication) demonstrated efficacy in participants with preexisting AAV5 NAb titers ≤678, showing durable FIX expression and reduced bleeding rates. This supports efficacy in the NCT06003387 population which specifically enrolls NAb-positive patients.

For NCT06003387 with n=35 estimated enrollment, single-arm design, no direct results available as trial is recruiting with primary completion expected October 2028. Predictions based on HOPE-B extrapolation to NAb-positive population.

Safety profile from HOPE-B: TEAEs common but manageable; ALT/AST elevations observed requiring corticosteroids in some patients; no treatment-related oncogenic events; infusion reactions infrequent; FIX inhibitors rare.

Key uncertainty: NAb-positive patients in NCT06003387 may show attenuated response compared to NAb-negative patients, though HOPE-B subgroup data suggests efficacy maintained at titers ≤678. Unknown proportion with high titers >678.

Efficacy endpoints (ABR, FIX activity, prophylaxis-free status) predicted to show clinically meaningful benefit based on HOPE-B data extrapolation. Safety endpoints predicted based on established AAV5 gene therapy profile.

Correlation analysis endpoint (secondary-22) is exploratory with no directional hypothesis specified in protocol; marked as partial with uncertainty regarding specific correlation coefficient magnitude.
Liver ultrasound changes (secondary-3) predicted to show no clinically significant changes based on HOPE-B 4-year data showing no late hepatotoxicity.
